summary: The Get started section of Business Central documentation introduces the product for learners, developers, and partners. It answers questions about what the product covers, building and publishing apps, selling and onboarding customers, common FAQs, and where to find help.
overview:
Get started is an entry point with no pages of its own. It is split into five subtopics: Learn, Develop, Sell, Frequently asked questions, and Help and support.

Learn is getting-started material: a business functionality overview, application design details, process walkthroughs, Contoso Coffee demo data for practice, and partner resources and communities. Develop (36 pages) is the largest subtopic. It covers building, customizing, publishing and maintaining apps and extensions. Sell covers how partners resell online, onboard customers, prepare company configuration packages, customize the application, and sell apps through Marketplace.

The FAQ gives short practical answers on AL development, app testing, marketplace submission, updating and marketing validation, library and dependency apps, migration to Business Central online, and the discontinued Windows client. Help and support (10 pages) is the subtopic to check for help resources.
key_points: Learn (6 pages) has a business functionality overview, application design details, process walkthroughs, Contoso Coffee demo data for practice, and pointers to partner resources and communities.

Develop (36 pages) covers building, customizing, publishing and maintaining apps and extensions, including getting started as a partner, Marketplace submission and validation, embed apps, app lifecycle, and localization.
Develop also explains which responsibilities belong to Microsoft and which to partners in Business Central online.

Sell (5 pages) covers reselling online, onboarding customers, company configuration packages, customizing the application, and selling apps through Marketplace, with answers on partner setup, licensing, and onboarding tools.

The FAQ (9 pages) gives short answers on AL development, app testing, marketplace submission, updating and marketing validation, library and dependency apps, migration to online, and the discontinued Windows client.
Help and support (10 pages) is the subtopic to check for help resources.

issues: The overview and the last key point include notes about the inputs ('no summary was provided', 'its content was not summarized') that don't help an agent reading the hub. Replaced with a neutral pointer to Help and support based on its title.
The FAQ coverage leaves out updating and marketing validation for the marketplace, which the FAQ summary lists. Restored.
'Learn is the best place for newcomers' is an opinion the inputs don't state. Changed it to describe Learn as getting-started material, which the Learn summary supports.
The Learn, Develop and Sell key points were each split in two. Merged so each subtopic has one clear point.
